implementation_notes: The platform primitive: a Channel<T> created unbounded defaults to SingleReader=false and supports any number of concurrent readers, each awaiting ReadAsync or ReadAllAsync and receiving exactly one item per read, so N consumer tasks compete without locks and without a broker. What the classic structure adds elsewhere - a dispatcher plus a worker pool class - is replaced by the channel's own synchronisation plus Task.WhenAll over the workers; bounded channels and FullMode give backpressure policy.
pitfalls: One shared ReadAllAsync loop is a pipeline, not competing consumers: every worker needs its own read loop over the same reader.
Blocking calls (Task.Wait, .Result, Thread.Sleep) inside a consumer starve the thread pool; keep the whole loop async.
Forgetting to call Writer.TryComplete/Complete leaves every ReadAllAsync awaiting forever, so shutdown hangs.

variants.name: TPL Dataflow ActionBlock (library)
variants.implementation_notes: For teams already on TPL Dataflow, an ActionBlock<T> with MaxDegreeOfParallelism = n is a complete competing-consumer pool: posted items queue inside the block and exactly one of the n concurrent tasks processes each item, with BoundedCapacity providing backpressure and Complete() the end-of-stream marker. It is the same mechanism as a channel plus workers, bought as a library with pipeline composition (link to other blocks) included.
pitfalls: MaxDegreeOfParallelism caps parallelism per block: linking a slow downstream block turns the whole pipeline into a bottleneck that extra consumers cannot widen.
SendAsync/Post returns before the item is processed; ignoring the completion task hides failures - always await Completion.
